text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ADEVARUL
- Romania has a foreign debt amounting to $7.0 billion but authorities have allegedly failed to use the funds properly, the paper says.
- Petrom RA oil company raised crude oil price by 5.9 percent to $108 a tonne.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Traffic on Danube River hampered by ice.
- Tender for Romania's third national television station might be scheduled for end-November, communications ministry director Andrei Bocsan said.
- New prices for energy will step up restructuring of Romania's big industrial sectors, Industry Ministry Calin Tariceanu says in interview.
CRONICA ROMANA
- Private petrol stations will be able to purchase directly from refineries up to 40 percent of their petrol output, the paper says.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Bucharest judge Constanta Taiatu is tried for forgery, embezzlement and fraud worth three billion lei.
- The church has the highest credibility rate of all state institutions in Romania, opinion survey shows.
- Tourism Ministry Akos Birtalan pledged to boost rural tourism and improve infrastructure by linking rural areas to automatic telephone exchanges.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- President Emil Constantinescu sacked army general Gheorghe Cheptine for alleged abuses and forgery. The case will be investigated by military prosecutors.
ADEVARUL

- The former ruling Party of Social Democracy ousted after November general elections to restructure on January 17. Ex-president Ion Iliescu will be elected party leader, but leadership jobs will be cut, newspaper says.
- Many of the Democratic Convention mayors failed to fulfill electoral promises in the bloc's 200-day contracts with the communities, newspaper says.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Romania is clearly on the right path to join NATO, U.S. Defence Under-Secretary for Policy Walter Slocombe told a news conference in Bucharest.
- Finance Ministry Mircea Ciumara said he launched a campaign to fight corruption among ministry staff.

- Communications minister plans to offer tender for nation-wide television licence for the country's third channel -- besides state television's two channels -- and it would cover up to 60 percent of Romania.
CRONICA ROMANA

- Newspaper editorial praises President Emil Constantinescu for his firm acts in fighting corruption. Constantinescu launched an unprecedented nationwide anti-corruption campaign and soon sacked a presidential adviser and an army general allegedly involved in cases of abuses and fraud. ($= 4,268 lei) -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
